# Components

Which components the system carries: its inventory, picked from the catalogue.

## The five answers

| Question | Answer | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which component families does it need? | Core, plus media | Campaigns lead with media and big sections. |
| How far does the inventory reach? | Only what today's screens use | One action and a story need only the parts in use; an agency keeps them fresh. |
| How does a component earn its place? | It gives the brand a moment | A component joins when it gives the campaign a moment. |
| When does a component get another look? | Also for emphasis and size | Variants for emphasis and size let each campaign look a little different. |
| Where do components do the most work? | Campaign sections | Components sit inside big campaign sections. |

## Where it lands

- Button
- Input
- Control
- Badge
- Card
- Table
- Tabs
- Overlay

## When to use what

| Situation | Use | Not | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No component in the inventory fits | a section built from the inventory with campaign tokens | a new component for one campaign | Campaigns change the look through tokens; new parts every drop are hard to keep working. |
